lessons.title: See before settings
lessons.observe: Name the relationship and the architectural device before touching a dial.
lessons.try: Watch one threshold for ten minutes and record five real verbs.
lessons.diagnose: If the frame needs a paragraph, simplify the relationship or move.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: An irrepeatable event requires immediate response.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Begin with a known exposure baseline, but let the scene choose the settings.
lessons.competition_note: Architecture must remain causal subject, not decorative background.

lessons.title: Position before focal length
lessons.observe: Walk until near/far relationships and verticals say what you mean.
lessons.try: Find three camera positions before selecting a lens.
lessons.diagnose: If layers collide or the background dominates, change position first.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Access or safety fixes the only legitimate position.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Use the 35–80 zoom as a scouting frame finder after choosing position.
lessons.competition_note: A non-default viewpoint must reveal a real relationship, not a gimmick.

lessons.title: Perspective vs field of view
lessons.observe: Camera position changes perspective; focal length changes field of view and framing from a fixed position.
lessons.try: Compare fixed position/different focal length, then fixed subject size/different position and focal length.
lessons.diagnose: If you say a lens compressed space, identify how camera distance changed.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Use shorthand only after the physical cause is understood.
lessons.canon_6d_note: 35, 50 and 85 mm share the same full-frame sensor reference.
lessons.competition_note: Choose the relation first and the crop second.

lessons.title: Depth, layering and figure-ground
lessons.observe: Separate foreground, architectural device, action and background.
lessons.try: Make one frame with three readable depth planes.
lessons.diagnose: If the person merges with an edge, wait or move laterally.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Flatness or silhouette is the intended formal idea.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Stop down only as far as the required planes demand.
lessons.competition_note: Depth should clarify the one-frame story.

lessons.title: Light reveals form and material
lessons.observe: Watch how light describes relief, texture, depth and use.
lessons.try: Revisit the same surface in hard light and garúa.
lessons.diagnose: If contrast hides the causal device, protect highlights or change time.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Silhouette or blown glare is essential to the idea.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Use histogram and highlight warnings; the meter is not artistic truth.
lessons.competition_note: Light must reveal architecture, not merely beautify it.

lessons.title: Composition beyond grids
lessons.observe: Ask what the viewer reads first, second and third.
lessons.try: Build hierarchy without a thirds overlay, then compare.
lessons.diagnose: If every element has equal weight, remove or reposition.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Tension, imbalance or ambiguity is the meaning.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Use the viewfinder edges as active compositional tools.
lessons.competition_note: Official creative/aesthetic coherence matters more than rule compliance.

lessons.title: Edge and background discipline
lessons.observe: Scan all four edges and every high-contrast background object.
lessons.try: Make one clean version before accepting clutter.
lessons.diagnose: If a pole grows from a person or signage steals attention, move centimeters.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Clutter is the architectural condition being shown.
lessons.canon_6d_note: The 6D viewfinder is not the final crop; inspect playback edges.
lessons.competition_note: Contest-safe editing makes in-camera edge control especially valuable.

lessons.title: Human gesture and decisive moment
lessons.observe: Find the verb that confirms or contradicts the design.
lessons.try: Pre-compose and wait for gesture to clear the architecture.
lessons.diagnose: If the person only supplies scale, the story is weak.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Meaningful absence carries stronger social evidence.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Set shutter for the intended gesture before lowering ISO.
lessons.competition_note: Never stage a false reality or bypass consent and ethics.

lessons.title: Meaningful absence
lessons.observe: Look for residue, expectation, furniture, wear and circulation without people.
lessons.try: Make structure readable as a social framework while empty.
lessons.diagnose: If emptiness says only clean architecture, search for lived evidence.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: A real human verb materially changes the meaning.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Use tripod-like discipline without assuming a tripod is permitted.
lessons.competition_note: The brief allows interiors, abstraction and inhabitation without forcing a person.

lessons.title: Exposure, metering and highlights
lessons.observe: Metering measures reflected light and proposes exposure; it does not know intent.
lessons.try: Compare evaluative reading with histogram and highlight warning.
lessons.diagnose: If important highlights clip, reduce exposure or change light.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Clipping is deliberate and supports the graphic idea.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Use exposure compensation or manual settings while reading the meter.
lessons.competition_note: Preserve print-relevant tonal information without illegal reconstruction.

lessons.title: Focus and sharpness fault tree
lessons.observe: Separate missed focus, camera shake, subject motion, insufficient DoF, optics/diffraction and atmosphere.
lessons.try: Change one cause at a time and review at useful magnification.
lessons.diagnose: Do not prescribe faster shutter when the fault is missed focus or heat haze.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Intentional blur carries the architectural or human motion.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Prefer the center AF point in difficult light and verify critical focus.
lessons.competition_note: Sharpness is a means to legibility, not an automatic aesthetic score.

lessons.title: ISO without superstition
lessons.observe: ISO supports the shutter and aperture the scene requires; there is no magic ISO.
lessons.try: Raise ISO to protect gesture, then compare with motion-blurred low ISO.
lessons.diagnose: Underexposure can be worse than a necessary higher ISO.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: A long exposure or intentional motion is the actual goal.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Choose ISO after required shutter and aperture, while monitoring highlights.
lessons.competition_note: A technically imperfect decisive frame may beat a clean empty one, but print viability remains.

lessons.title: DoF versus bokeh separation
lessons.observe: Subject DoF and background blur/separation are related but distinct.
lessons.try: Hold focal, aperture and focus distance fixed while changing background distance.
lessons.diagnose: If DoF stays fixed but background rendering changes, the model is working.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Describe the visible outcome plainly in fast field use.
lessons.canon_6d_note: The Optical Lab uses CoC 0.030 mm as a planning convention.
lessons.competition_note: Use separation only when it clarifies architectural causality.

lessons.title: Work the scene
lessons.observe: Notice how action, edges and light cycle rather than taking one frame and leaving.
lessons.try: Make A structure, B habitar, C anti-postal, D light/material and E one-frame story proofs.
lessons.diagnose: Log why the strongest attempt still fails.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: The event is unsafe, unethical or genuinely finished.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Keep settings stable long enough to diagnose composition separately.
lessons.competition_note: Choose STAY, MOVE or RETURN_OTHER_LIGHT from evidence.

lessons.title: Garúa, rain, noon and blue hour
lessons.observe: Treat weather and difficult hours as different form-making tools.
lessons.try: Use garúa for soft material separation and noon for hard graphic shadows.
lessons.diagnose: If conditions add atmosphere but hide architecture, change the hypothesis.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Safety, access or equipment protection requires leaving.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Use IS where appropriate, protect the camera, and set shutter from subject intent.
lessons.competition_note: Do not default to golden hour; use the condition that reveals the relationship.

lessons.title: Anti-dogma
lessons.observe: Rules are diagnostic prompts, not guarantees.
lessons.try: Make the conventional solution, then one evidence-based contradiction.
lessons.diagnose: If rule breaking has no visible purpose, it is novelty without meaning.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: The scene communicates more clearly or truthfully without it.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Technique serves the frame, not camera ritual.
lessons.competition_note: Originality never overrides theme coherence or photographed reality.

lessons.title: Contest-safe editing boundaries
lessons.observe: Decide whether the frame works before imagining post-production rescue.
lessons.try: Plan for crop, white balance, B&W, brightness, contrast, sharpness and color correction only.
lessons.diagnose: Any change to fundamental elements, AI intervention, collage or altered reality fails the safety gate.
lessons.break_the_rule_when: Do not break this rule for a competition submission.
lessons.canon_6d_note: Level, position and frame carefully in camera because transform legality is not explicit.
lessons.competition_note: Keep the candidate RAW/JPG/JPEG outside AI critique and editing; preflight is deterministic and local.
